implication: Informs twin labor contracts by binding verifiable credential proofs directly to resource budgets and past outcome provenance.

title: Copies or Sources? Measuring How LLM Aggregators Count Restated Evidence in Multi-Agent Systems
summary: In multi-agent systems, language model aggregators often mistake forwarded copies for independent evidence (copy weight 0.06 to 0.42). Requiring agents to reference canonical reading identifiers rather than restating text reduces early false commitments from 11.2% to 1.1% while preserving genuine corroboration.
implication: Deliberation summarizers and consensus engines must track distinct source references rather than raw message repeats, preventing information cascades from masquerading as consensus.

title: The Cognitive Firewall: Securing Browser-Based AI Agents Against Indirect Prompt Injection via Hybrid Edge-Cloud Defense
summary: Proposes Cognitive Firewall, a split-compute architecture with local edge visual filtering and deterministic execution guards to defeat indirect prompt injections with sub-1% attack success rate.
implication: Informs personal assistant design: pairing deterministic execution guards with local filtering keeps side-effect boundaries robust and prevents unauthorized actions.

title: Privacy Practices of Browser Agents
summary: Systematically evaluates eight popular browser agents across 15 measurements, uncovering 30 vulnerabilities including disabled browser privacy controls and unsafe autocompletion of sensitive data.
implication: Highlights the critical risk of autonomous web agents leaking private context or bypassing browser privacy controls without strict personal boundaries.

title: AMBER: Training Long-Horizon Web Agents through Append-Only Memory
summary: An append-only memory framework for long-horizon web agents guarantees fact and error feedback retention by construction, preventing the catastrophic forgetting and context deletion typical of overwrite memories.
implication: Agent architectures for browser tasks and personal interfaces benefit from immutable append-only logs of environment interactions and feedback rather than destructive summarization or state overwriting.

title: Safeguarding LLMs via Model-Agnostic Latent Safety Signals from Dark Knowledge
summary: Contrasting output probabilities in the first-token distribution reveals model-agnostic latent safety directions that defend against jailbreaks without internal architecture access.
implication: Provides a model-agnostic mechanism to detect adversarial queries at decoding time via token probability shifts without requiring intrusive model weights or architecture hooks.

title: Sparse Feature Policy Unlearning Mitigates State Hallucination in Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: Sparse autoencoders identify interpretable features linked to state hallucination in embodied agents; selective unlearning removes hallucination failures while preserving core capabilities.
implication: Demonstrates that mechanistic sparse feature identification can pinpoint failure modes in multi-step agents and guide targeted policy unlearning without wholesale retraining.

title: From Observation to Intervention: Identifiability of Latent User Bias in Human-AI Interaction
summary: Formalizes failure modes when alignment methods treat user behavior as an unbiased proxy for preferences, showing cognitive confirmation bias traps models in reinforcing mistaken user beliefs without active interventional probing.
implication: Personal agents cannot treat passive user behavior as ground-truth preference signals without falling into feedback loops that amplify cognitive biases.

title: Extracting Illicit-Rich Subgraph from Transaction Networks via Feed-Guided Shortest Paths
summary: Evaluates seed-selection heuristics for subgraph extraction in financial transaction graphs, demonstrating that centrality-guided shortest paths isolate illicit transaction clusters without dense global graph traversals.
implication: Auditing distributed transaction networks can bound investigative computation to localized subgraphs around suspicious flow clusters.

title: Calibration in One Go: Jointly Learning Accurate and Calibrated Neural Networks
summary: Proposes an integrated training loss that optimizes predictive accuracy and probability calibration jointly, eliminating the need for post-hoc validation datasets while achieving lower expected calibration error.
implication: Decision gates and risk monitors can obtain reliable calibrated probability estimates directly from runtime classifiers without separate post-hoc calibration splits.

title: Variance-Reduced Policy Gradient is Nearly Minimax-Optimal
summary: Proves that variance-reduced policy gradient algorithms achieve nearly minimax-optimal sample complexity under Markov decision processes without requiring uniform importance weight bounds.
implication: Reinforcement learning training in agent simulations can achieve sample-efficient convergence without brittle importance sampling assumptions.

title: Entropy Regularization under No-Shorting: Structure Preservation and Convexity in Dynamic Mean-Variance Portfolio Selection
summary: Establishes dynamic mean-variance portfolio allocation under no-shorting constraints using entropy regularization, proving policy convexity and stable numerical updates without unbounded leverage.
implication: Multi-asset liquidity pools and reserve mechanisms can enforce non-negative balances while preserving convex, tractable dynamic rebalancing.

title: Know What You Don't Know: Agentic Data Synthesis by Evolving Generation Space for Closed-Loop Learning
summary: Proposes closed-loop synthetic environment generation that dynamically targets model deficiencies, synthesizing verifiable multi-agent trajectories that optimize learning progression.
implication: Multi-agent simulation platforms can dynamically generate focused edge-case scenarios based on discovered behavioral failures.

title: What Counts as Evidence? Epistemic Cue Utilization in Large Language Models
summary: Evaluates how models weigh competing evidence across source, temporal, and presentation cues, finding that recognizing source reliability does not reliably prevent models from being swayed by presentation style.
implication: Deliberation platforms cannot rely on models to objectively weigh conflicting evidence without structured provenance checks and explicit calibration.

title: CLEAT: Learning Value-Guided Clarification for Interactive Agents
summary: Co-trains a clarification-value controller and agent policy using residual query value from paired rollouts, improving interactive intent alignment under underspecification.
implication: Provides a principled, measurable criterion for when personal agents should pause to query users versus executing autonomously under underspecified goals.

title: SpireBench: Evaluating Long-Horizon Strategic Play of Agentic Models with Slay the Spire
summary: Evaluates 20 LLMs on long-horizon strategic play in Slay the Spire; finds frontier models fall behind experts over long horizons and fail to improve from cross-run memories.
implication: Challenges assumptions that cross-run agent memory automatically improves long-horizon strategic decisions, demonstrating risk-misjudgment and memory degradation.

title: SoK: Privacy-Preserving Order Matching
summary: Systematizes 22 privacy-preserving order matching protocol families across four order lifecycle phases, establishing that protecting individual phases fails to prevent end-to-end information leakage.
implication: Value exchange and allocation mechanisms in the network must enforce holistic lifecycle privacy across submission, matching, and settlement rather than isolated phase encryption.

title: PVBRF-ID: Private, Verifiable and Byzantine-Robust Federated Intrusion Detection for Oilfield Enterprise Networks
summary: Presents a two-server federated protocol where participants secret-share updates to jointly test cosine similarity and norm against a reference without exposing updates in the clear.
implication: Federated agent training and simulation aggregation can verify update integrity and resist Byzantine poisoning without requiring nodes to pool raw operational updates.

title: SCCGBench: Executability-Oriented Evaluation for Real-World Web Service-Call Code Generation
summary: Evaluates code generation for service invocations across 3,135 functions, finding models generate superficially plausible calls but the strongest model achieves only 3.76% executability without documentation oracles.
implication: Agents cannot reliably synthesize API or tool interactions from intent alone; deterministic schemas and host-verified endpoint definitions are necessary.

title: On the Fragility of AI Agent Collusion
summary: In repeated pricing with LLM agents, heterogeneity in patience and data access reduces collusive price lift from 22% to 10% and 7%, while cross-algorithm mixing breaks collusion; model-size differences stabilize it.
implication: CIN task-allocation and multi-agent verification markets must deliberately introduce cross-algorithm and cadence heterogeneity rather than uniform LLM agent architectures to prevent spontaneous tacit collusion.
